post.summary:
A local install's only (FAILED_PRECONDITION elsewhere): looks again for
the install's default on its machine (FoundryAI.detected), as Settings ›
AI models opens, so a model pulled since is used without a restart.

get.summary:
A local install's only (FAILED_PRECONDITION elsewhere): the models an
Ollama server has, for the Ollama card's model choice.

post.summary:
Helix Foundry event sources: connectors of kind events, made, changed and
deleted through the connector routes. No route sends pieces.

get.summary:
Helix Foundry documents and document sets, the workspace's: the Data
area.

parameters.name: setId
parameters.description: Only this set's documents, uploads or a connector's, when set.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Only these documents, uploads or a connector's, deleted or not, in this
order, on one page: at most 100, with no set_id or page_token
(INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). An id the workspace has no document for
is left out.

post.summary:
Helix Foundry ontologies, each bound to one tenant database. Deleting one
leaves its database as it is.

get.summary:
An ontology's documents, read only: what its current load holds and
what its reading version's scope holds, each with its extraction there.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only those the current load holds so: waiting (not extracted yet),
extracted, review (extracted, with reviews), duplicate, failed or
out_of_scope; empty for all.

post.summary:
The ontology-scoped document and set writes, and the set list, from
before documents were the workspace's: aliases of the routes above,
with the same workspace semantics, kept for the website still on them
until release 2 of workspace documents removes them.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: Only this thread's questions; empty lists all.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: Last decision id from a previous page.

get.summary: Helix Foundry usage: the workspace's AI spend this month, by task
get.description:
The UTC calendar month's spend of loads, of API sources' extraction no
person started, and of questions, each with its cap: the sums the caps
check. Spend on the workspace's own model key counts, as Helix's monthly
caps count it. Any member may read it.

loadId.description: The load to ask; empty asks the current one.

threadId.description: A question of this ontology starting the thread to continue; empty starts one.

FoundryServiceAskFoundryQuestionBody.description:
AskFoundryQuestionRequest queues a question of a ready or partial load
(FAILED_PRECONDITION otherwise, or when the workspace has spent this
month's questions budget; RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED past its questions an hour).
The same client_token returns the question it queued.

FoundryServiceCancelFoundryQuestionBody.description:
CancelFoundryQuestionRequest ends a queued or running question; a running
one is charged what it reserved. One that ended otherwise is
FAILED_PRECONDITION.

FoundryServiceCompleteFoundryDocumentUpl.description:
CompleteFoundryDocumentUploadRequest checks the bytes PUT to the upload
URL and marks the document uploaded. Every ontology whose live or current
load reads its set then reads it, where the caller may write the
ontology's database; reads says what happened for each.

name.description:
1 to 255 characters once trimmed, with no slash, backslash or control
character; its extension must agree with media_type: .md or .markdown
text/markdown, .mdx text/mdx, .txt text/plain, .json application/json,
.csv text/csv, .tsv text/tab-separated-values, .jsonl or .ndjson
application/x-ndjson, .parquet application/vnd.apache.parquet, .pdf
application/pdf.

clientToken.description: Makes the create idempotent per workspace.

setId.description: A live document set of the workspace.

name.description:
1 to 120 characters, unique among the workspace's live sets (case and
accents aside).

description.description:
What its documents hold, in the user's words; at most 1000 characters.
The ontology agent reads it.

FoundryServiceCreateFoundryLoadBody.description:
CreateFoundryLoadRequest writes an agent draft whose status is done into
the ontology's database as a new load, beside the loads already there. A
delete in progress gives way and resumes after it; FAILED_PRECONDITION while
a load or extract is live, or the month's budget is spent.

tenantId.description:
A live tenant of one of the workspace's projects, which the caller may
write: one from GET /v1/tenants, or one just made with POST /v1/tenants.

clientToken.description: Makes the create idempotent: the same token returns the same ontology.

FoundryServiceCreateFoundryOntologyDocum.description:
The ontology-scoped aliases' requests (until release 2 of workspace
documents): as the workspace routes', with the ontology of the route,
which must be a live ontology of the workspace (NOT_FOUND otherwise), as
before documents were the workspace's.

goal.description: What the ontology should serve, in the user's words; at most 2000 characters.

connectorIds.description:
The connectors whose synced tables to draft from; empty means all,
unless no_connectors.

documentSetIds.description:
The document sets the draft reads, which become its version's scope;
empty means none. At most 20: INVALID_ARGUMENT past that. Each set's
table files that have been read (CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL, Parquet) are
tables beside the connectors' (files still being read are left out),
and its Markdown, MDX and text may be routed to extraction.
A generation needs at least one source: a synced table, a table file,
or a set holding text (FAILED_PRECONDITION without one). Tables and
table files together count toward the deployment's cap on tables.

noConnectors.description:
Draft from the document sets alone, with no connector, even when the
workspace has some; connector_ids must then be empty (INVALID_ARGUMENT
otherwise).

eventSources.description:
Event sources to draft from, each with how this ontology reads it.
connector_ids names no event source, and its empty default never
includes one. Extraction reads the source's own document set, which
counts as one of the 20 sets, and needs the source to have a
text_field and a synced piece (FAILED_PRECONDITION without either).

sample.description:
Foundry's sample company to draft from in place of the AI: "acme" is
the only one (INVALID_ARGUMENT for another). The generation stores the
sample's ready-made draft, mapped to this workspace's connection to the
sample's database, and calls no model. connector_ids must name exactly
that connection and document_set_ids exactly the set of the sample's
documents, with no event source (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise), and each
of the sample's tables must be synced (FAILED_PRECONDITION until then).

FoundryServiceMoveFoundryDocumentBody.description:
MoveFoundryDocumentRequest puts a document in another live set of the
workspace. A load keeps what it read: the move applies to it from the next
load. An uploaded document is then read as an upload into the set is.

layout.description: The website's JSON object, at most 64 KiB; stored as it is.

expectedRevision.description: The revision read; 0 for a workspace with none yet.

FoundryServicePutFoundryDataLayoutBody.description:
PutFoundryDataLayoutRequest replaces the layout the caller read:
FAILED_PRECONDITION when expected_revision is no longer the workspace's.

FoundryServiceReadFoundryGraphBody.description:
ReadFoundryGraphRequest reads a load of the ontology's database: entities
with the facts its version's rules derive, patterns, explanations ("why"),
rule breaks and evidence. reads_json is a JSON array of 1 to 20 reads, each
the `reads` item of the ontology agent's read_request.json. NOT_FOUND for a
load of another ontology or one deleted; FAILED_PRECONDITION while it is
being deleted; RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED while the workspace has as many reads
running as it may.

FoundryServiceSetCurrentFoundryLoadBody.description:
SetCurrentFoundryLoadRequest points the ontology's reads and uploads at a
ready or partial load (FAILED_PRECONDITION otherwise). Documents it lacks
are extracted into it: at once, or after the live job.

expectedCurrentVersionId.description: The version the caller saw as current; empty for none. A mismatch is FailedPrecondition.

FoundryServiceSettleFoundryReviewBody.description: Reads the current load's review. Stores a decision for the next load only.

FoundryServiceStopFoundryLoadEnrichmentB.description:
StopFoundryLoadEnrichmentRequest stops a load's lookups: a queued step
ends at once, a running one after its batch; the load then applies what
was found. NOT_FOUND when the load has no step.

full.description: Read every table in full, even where changes could be read.

config.description: Replaces settings and credentials together; they are tested before saving.

syncEverySeconds.description:
0 returns to the plan's interval, -1 turns automatic syncs off, and a
positive value syncs that often, never below the plan's shortest.

models.description: Unset models get the kind's suggestions.

apiKey.description: Blank keeps the setting's key where it still belongs to the endpoint.

FoundryServiceUpdateFoundryAIBody.description:
UpdateFoundryAIRequest is an owner's change: back to the default at once,
or a provider saved and tested before it is used (FoundryAI.pending);
the setting in force stays until the test passes. Bringing a key needs
Foundry Pro or Max when hosted (FAILED_PRECONDITION, reason
FOUNDRY_PRO_REQUIRED); a model Helix can't price needs rates
(FAILED_PRECONDITION, reason FOUNDRY_AI_PRICE_REQUIRED); saves are capped
per hour (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED).

name.description:
1 to 255 characters once trimmed, with no slash, backslash or control
character.

FoundryServiceUpdateFoundryDocumentBody.description: UpdateFoundryDocumentRequest renames a document that is not deleted.

FoundryServiceUpdateFoundryDocumentSetBo.description: UpdateFoundryDocumentSetRequest changes what is set of name and description.

noticeVersion.description: The notice the owner was shown.

FoundryServiceUpdateFoundryEnrichmentBod.description:
UpdateFoundryEnrichmentRequest records an owner's change, kept as history
with the notice they were shown. Turning it on needs Helix's flag
(FAILED_PRECONDITION) and Foundry Pro (FAILED_PRECONDITION, reason
FOUNDRY_PRO_REQUIRED); turning it off is always allowed: running lookups
are cancelled, stored profiles deleted, and each ontology whose loads
applied some is loaded again without them.

autoRefresh.description: Whether a changed table reloads the current version by itself.

protobufNullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
`Value` type union.

The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.

apiKey.description: Cal.com API key (cal_live_… or cal_…); write-only.

secretHint.description: Identifies the stored credential without revealing it, e.g. sk_live…4f2a.

tables.description: Tables the last syncs copied, each pointing at its newest snapshot.

cdcStatus.description: Set while the connector reads a database's log.

position.description: The PostgreSQL slot, or the MySQL binlog position.

retainedBytes.description: Bytes of WAL the slot holds on the customer's database; PostgreSQL only.

events.description: 11 and 12 are gdrive's and gmail's (Google connectors).

v1ConnectorConfig.description: ConnectorConfig is a connector's settings. Write-only fields come back empty.

unavailable.description:
Objects the source has but the connector cannot read, as name or
"name: reason".

maxBytes.description: File sources: the stored-byte limit across the tables one sync reads.

warnings.description: Settings that work but cost the customer, each worded with its fix.

v1ConnectorDiscovery.description: ConnectorDiscovery is what a source exposes to the connector's credential.

kind.description:
stripe, workos, posthog, github, linear, calcom, granola, postgres, mysql,
s3 or events.

available.description: False when the workspace's plan does not include the kind.

planCode.description: The lowest catalog plan that includes the kind.

v1ConnectorKind.description: ConnectorKind is one type of Helix Foundry data source.

v1ConnectorResponse.description: ConnectorResponse carries discovery only when the call tested the credential.

everySeconds.description: The owner's choice; 0 means the plan's interval, -1 manual only.

effectiveEverySeconds.description: The interval in force, after the plan's limits; 0 when manual only.

pausedReason.description: Why automatic syncs stopped; empty while they run.

v1ConnectorSchedule.description: ConnectorSchedule is when a connector syncs by itself.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, written for the customer.

nextAttemptAt.description: When a queued sync runs next; later than now while a retry waits.

v1ConnectorSync.description: ConnectorSync is one run copying a connector's tables into snapshots.

columns.description: Empty for API sources until their first sync.

format.description:
File sources only, from here on.
parquet, json or csv.

bytes.description: Stored bytes of the table's files.

preview.description: At most 5 rows, each one JSON object.

problem.description: Why a sample could not be read; the sync fails until it is fixed.

v1ConnectorTableChange.description: ConnectorTableChange is one sync's change to one table.

upload.description: Unset when the document is already uploaded.

existing.description:
The workspace already had this document: the same client token, or the
same bytes in whatever set it is (document.set_id), which may not be the
set asked for.

secret.description: The token, hx_ev_ and 64 hex digits: returned this once and never stored.

routed.description:
Whether the ontology's reading version has the document's set in scope
and its routes name it. The set list's read_by says it for every
ontology.

clientToken.description: Per-click token. Two calls carrying the same token are one purchase.

promoCode.description: Stripe promotion code the customer typed; optional.

planCode.description: A catalog plan's code, from ListFoundryPlans; wins over tier when set.

checkoutUrl.description:
The checkout page to send the customer to; empty when the billing system
charged a card on file.

plan.description:
The plan now. It can read FREE for a moment after a charge; read
GetFoundryPlan again.

publication.description: PostgreSQL: the publication the customer created; empty means helix_foundry.

serverId.description: MySQL: the replica server id; 0 derives one from the connector.

tables.description: Tables to sync; empty means every table.

ca.description: PEM bundle trusted besides the system roots.

cursorColumns.description:
Table to the column its application updates on every write; a change
sync reads only rows past the column's last value.

cdc.description: Change data capture from the database's log; plans with log capture only.

rows.description: Rows in its table plus pieces not synced yet (resent ids count again).

bytes.description: Uncompressed bytes of its table plus those of batches not synced yet.

v1EventSourceCapacity.description:
EventSourceCapacity is how full an event source's table is, against the
caps every table has. Output only.

type.description: string, number, boolean, object or array; null while it has only been null.

description.description:
What each piece is, for people and Foundry's agent; at most 1000
characters. Absent on update leaves it unchanged.

fields.description:
Output only: the top-level fields its pieces have carried, by name, each
with the JSON type it holds. Ignored on create and update.

textField.description:
The top-level field holding each piece's text: the body of the piece's
document in the source's own set, which entity extraction reads. It
names a field the pieces have carried as a string (or only as null), or
one they have not carried yet, and locks it as a string: later pieces
must comply. Absent on update leaves it unchanged; "" clears it, and the
source then has no documents and no extraction. Changing it re-renders
the newest pieces in one full sync.

v1EventsConnectorConfig.description:
EventsConnectorConfig is an event source: pieces of data, JSON objects
with an id, that people and their agents send to Foundry. It has no
credential.

active.description: The provider in force; unset is the default.

default.description:
The deployment's provider; unset is none, which only a local install
has: model work is then refused (FOUNDRY_AI_NOT_CONFIGURED) until an
owner chooses one.

pending.description: A save waiting for or in its test.

lastFailed.description: The newest save, when its test failed after the setting last changed.

privateHostsAllowed.description: Endpoints may be http and private addresses: a local install.

proRequired.description:
The workspace's plan doesn't include bringing a key: saving one is
refused (FAILED_PRECONDITION, reason FOUNDRY_PRO_REQUIRED) until it is
on Foundry Pro or Max. Going back to the default never is.

detected.description:
How a local install that names no default provider found one on its
machine (default, when it found one); unset hosted, and in an install
whose FOUNDRY_AI_PROVIDER names its default.

v1FoundryAI.description: FoundryAI is a workspace's AI setting.

v1FoundryAIAzureOpenAI.description: An Azure OpenAI resource; each model's name is a deployment's.

v1FoundryAIBedrock.description: Amazon Bedrock, called with a Bedrock API key.

v1FoundryAICompatAPI.description: FoundryAICompatAPI is the API an OpenAI-compatible server speaks.

keyHint.description: Which key it was saved with, e.g. sk-ant…4f2a; empty for none.

hasKey.description: Whether the key is still stored: only the setting's and a pending one's are.

probeFailure.description:
Why a failed probe failed: an agent ModelFailure (auth, not_found, ...)
and its check's ProbeDetail (tools_rejected, ...).

label.description: The provider as failure copy names it: "Claude", or a custom server's host.

v1FoundryAIConfig.description: FoundryAIConfig is a provider an owner saved.

summary.description:
For the owner: what is used and why, or what was looked for and how to
set a provider up. Never a key.

v1FoundryAIDetected.description:
FoundryAIDetected is how a local install found its default, looking in
this order: an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then an OPENAI_API_KEY, in its
environment; an Ollama it can reach (the bundled one, then this
computer's) with a model that calls tools; LM Studio on this computer
serving a model. It looks again as Settings › AI models opens
(DetectFoundryAIDefault).

v1FoundryAIKey.description:
FoundryAIKey is whether a kind's calls carry an API key.

 - FOUNDRY_AI_KEY_NONE: Ollama's native API takes none.

v1FoundryAIKind.description:
FoundryAIKind is a model provider kind. Every kind is declared; a
deployment offers those its agent implements (FoundryAI.offered).

table.description:
Helix's price table for the model (FAILED_PRECONDITION, reason
FOUNDRY_AI_PRICE_REQUIRED, when it has none).

tableAs.description:
Helix's price table for another model of the same kind: an Azure
deployment's underlying model, or a Bedrock inference profile's.

free.description: No cost counted: Ollama and OpenAI-compatible servers only.

v1FoundryAIModel.description: FoundryAIModel is a model and how its calls are priced.

v1FoundryAIModels.description:
FoundryAIModels is a model per task: drafting ontologies, answering
questions, reading documents and checking the facts read.

suggested.description:
The models a save of the kind gets where it names none; unset for a
kind whose owner names every model.

v1FoundryAIOffer.description: FoundryAIOffer is a kind an owner may choose.

contextTokens.description: The context window models load with; 0 is 65536.

v1FoundryAIOllama.description: An Ollama server's native API, which takes no key.

v1FoundryAIProbeState.description:
FoundryAIProbeState is where a saved provider is in its test.

 - FOUNDRY_AI_PROBE_STATE_SUPERSEDED: Replaced by a newer save, or by going back to the default, first.

v1FoundryAIProvider.description:
FoundryAIProvider is where a workspace's model calls go: one message per
kind, holding that kind's endpoint settings and never a key.

cachedInputUsdPerMtok.description: Empty when cached input is not priced apart.

v1FoundryAIRates.description:
FoundryAIRates are prices in US dollars per million tokens, as decimal
strings with at most three decimals ("0.075").

sold.description: False for Free and for a plan the deployment does not sell.

v1FoundryCatalogPlan.description: FoundryCatalogPlan is one plan the deployment's catalog offers.

layout.description: {} for a workspace with none yet.

revision.description: How many writes it has had: 0 for none.

v1FoundryDataLayoutResponse.description: FoundryDataLayoutResponse is how the workspace's Data tree is arranged.

mediaType.description:
text/markdown, text/mdx, text/plain, application/json, text/csv,
text/tab-separated-values, application/x-ndjson,
application/vnd.apache.parquet or application/pdf. A rename keeps it.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes.

status.description:
pending_upload, uploaded or deleted. A connector's document is only
uploaded or deleted: deleted once replaced or removed at its source.

extraction.description:
Read through an ontology's routes: what extracting it into that
ontology's current load made of it; unset until then, while no load is
current, and on the workspace's routes.

setId.description: The document set it belongs to.

ontologies.description:
The ontologies associated with it, on the workspace's GET only: those
whose current load holds it, and those whose reading version (the
current load's, else the current version) has its set in scope.

read.description:
How ontologies read it, and what reading it has come to; unset until
its upload completes.

source.description: The row of a connector's table it is the text of; unset for an upload.

v1FoundryDocument.description:
FoundryDocument is one document of a workspace, in one of its document
sets: one a person uploaded, or the text of one row of a connector's table
(source), which the connector's syncs write into its set. Ontologies read
text/markdown, text/mdx (as Markdown, with its code blanked to spaces; it
is never compiled or run) and text/plain as text, extracted through
routes. Each text/csv,
text/tab-separated-values, application/json, application/x-ndjson and
application/vnd.apache.parquet document is read once, at upload, as a
table of its own, which a version's mappings name by the document's id; it
is never extracted. Each application/pdf document is read once, at
upload, to its text (read), and is extracted through routes as that text
once read; a scanned PDF has no text to read.

status.description:
extracted, duplicate, failed or out_of_scope: no extraction route of the
load's version names its set, so it is stored with its sections and no
model read it.

duplicateOf.description: The document whose text this one repeats, for duplicate.

v1FoundryDocumentExtraction.description: FoundryDocumentExtraction is how a document ended in its ontology's database.

routed.description:
Whether the routes of the ontology's reading version name the
document's set: its documents are read for what they hold, not only
stored.

extraction.description:
What extracting it into the ontology's current load made of it; unset
when that load has not extracted it, or there is none.

v1FoundryDocumentOntology.description: FoundryDocumentOntology is one ontology a document is associated with.

v1FoundryDocumentRead.description: FoundryDocumentRead is the outcome for one ontology.

v1FoundryDocumentReadOutcome.description:
What completing or moving a document did for one ontology that reads its
set: one whose live job's load, or current load, is of a version with the
set in scope.

 - FOUNDRY_DOCUMENT_READ_OUTCOME_QUEUED: An extract of the document into the current load was queued.
 - FOUNDRY_DOCUMENT_READ_OUTCOME_OWED: A job of the ontology is live: it reads the document, or its end
queues the extract that does.
 - FOUNDRY_DOCUMENT_READ_OUTCOME_NO_BUDGET: Nothing was queued: the workspace spent this month's budget. The next
load or extract reads it.
 - FOUNDRY_DOCUMENT_READ_OUTCOME_HELD: Nothing was queued: the current load already holds the document (a
move), and keeps what it read until the next load.
 - FOUNDRY_DOCUMENT_READ_OUTCOME_SKIPPED: Nothing was queued or owed: the caller may not write the ontology's
database (database.query.write on its project). A later load or extract
reads it.
 - FOUNDRY_DOCUMENT_READ_OUTCOME_READING: Nothing was queued yet: the document is a PDF whose text is still being
read. The load holds it, and the read's end has the ontology read it
(queued, or owed by a live job).

reads.description: One per ontology whose live or current load reads the document's set.

description.description: What its documents hold, in the user's words; empty when none was given.

documents.description: Its documents that are not deleted.

readBy.description:
The ontologies whose reading version (the current load's, else the
current version) has it in scope, on lists.

connector.description: The connector whose syncs write the set; unset for a set a person made.

v1FoundryDocumentSet.description:
FoundryDocumentSet is a named group of a workspace's documents: a folder
of the Data tree. Every document belongs to one set. A version reads the
sets of its scope, and its extraction routes ([extractions.<name>] in its
mappings) name, by id, the sets whose documents they read for what they
hold. A person makes a set, or a connector's syncs do (connector).

stream.description: The kind's name for what the set holds (notes); it never changes.

maxDocuments.description:
The most documents a sync of everything keeps: the newest at the
source. A sync of changes may add past it until the next one, except
in an API source's set, which never holds more.

connectorName.description: The connector's name when the set was read.

connectorKind.description: The connector's kind (granola, events); it never changes.

monthSystemUsdMicros.description:
What work no person started (refreshes, and extracts no one asked for)
has spent extracting the set's documents in the current UTC month, in
millionths of a US dollar. Read only for a set with an allowance; 0
for any other.

paused.description:
Whether the set's syncs write no documents now: it holds some, and work
no person started can spend no more extracting it this UTC month (its
allowance, its workspace's for all its API sources, or the workspace's
month's share for such work is spent). The graph keeps the pieces it
extracted; the newest wait for next month, or for a load a person
starts, and a sync a person starts still writes them. False for a set
without an allowance.

v1FoundryDocumentSetConnector.description:
FoundryDocumentSetConnector is the connector and stream a set holds the
documents of: one set per connector and stream, for as long as the
connector lives. The set and its documents are the connector's: changing
or deleting the set, and uploading, moving or deleting its documents, is
FAILED_PRECONDITION; what it holds changes with the connection's
settings. Its name is the stream's title ("Notes"), and the user calls it
"<connector_name> / <name>". It takes no place among the workspace's
document sets or their names, and its documents none in the workspace's
uploads; a generation's pick of sets counts it.

routed.description: Whether the reading version's routes name the set.

v1FoundryDocumentSetReader.description: FoundryDocumentSetReader is an ontology that reads a document set.

externalId.description:
The key of its row at the source (a Granola note's id), unique among
its set's documents that are not deleted.

version.description: The source's version of the row's text.

url.description:
The item's page at the source, an absolute https URL; empty when it
has none.

at.description:
The item's own time at the source (a note's creation), which orders the
set's documents, newest first.

v1FoundryDocumentSource.description:
FoundryDocumentSource is where a connector's document comes from. The
document is the connector's: renaming, moving or deleting it is
FAILED_PRECONDITION. New text at the source is a new document that
replaces it; a new version with the same text changes it in place.

v1FoundryDocumentUpload.description:
FoundryDocumentUpload is a presigned PUT of a document's bytes. Send exactly
the declared bytes with these headers before expires_at; the browser adds
Content-Length, which is signed too.

enabled.description: The owner's consent to look the workspace's people up on context.dev.

monthlyCreditCap.description:
The most credits the workspace's loads charge in a calendar month (UTC);
0 until an owner sets it.

creditsUsed.description: Credits charged this month, unanswered calls included.

creditsReserved.description: Credits a running load holds for its lookups.

capResetsAt.description: When the month's credits start again: the first of next month, UTC.

enabledBy.description: The owner who turned it on, and when; unset while it is off.

purgesPending.description:
Ontologies whose enriched values a clean load has still to remove,
since consent was turned off.

v1FoundryEnrichment.description: FoundryEnrichment is a workspace's People enrichment setting and month.

v1FoundryEnrichmentAvailability.description:
FoundryEnrichmentAvailability is whether a workspace's loads may look
people up.

 - FOUNDRY_ENRICHMENT_AVAILABILITY_UNSPECIFIED: Helix can't say for now: the workspace's plan couldn't be read. Turning
People enrichment off still works.
 - FOUNDRY_ENRICHMENT_AVAILABILITY_DISABLED: Helix has People enrichment off: loads look no one up, and apply the
profiles found before.
 - FOUNDRY_ENRICHMENT_AVAILABILITY_PRO_REQUIRED: New lookups need Foundry Pro; the profiles found before still apply.

synced.description: A sync has read it: its pieces are in the source's table.

v1FoundryEventSourceMode.description:
FoundryEventSourceMode is how a generation reads an event source.

 - FOUNDRY_EVENT_SOURCE_MODE_STRUCTURED: Its table, through mappings: pieces reach the graph when the ontology refreshes.
 - FOUNDRY_EVENT_SOURCE_MODE_EXTRACTION: Its pieces as text documents of its own set, extracted as they arrive.

v1FoundryEventSourcePick.description:
FoundryEventSourcePick is one event source a generation drafts from, and
how its ontology reads it.

v1FoundryEventSourceToken.description: FoundryEventSourceToken is a send-only credential of one event source.

code.description:
too_large, unsupported, model or store. A PDF whose read failed is
recorded with the read's code; the document's read says why.

retryable.description: Whether a later load may succeed.

rows.description: A table file's rows, once read.

mode.description: The read shown, for a table file or a PDF; unset for text.

error.description: Why it can't be read, exactly when FAILED.

retrying.description:
A READING read that failed for a reason that is not the file's (such as
storage) and waits to be read again.

v1FoundryFileRead.description:
FoundryFileRead is how ontologies read a document, and what reading it
has come to.

code.description:
too_large (past a reading limit: a PDF of more than 150 pages, or whose
text is past 1 MiB) or unsupported (not what its type says; a PDF that
is damaged, encrypted, or scanned with no text, whose message is
"Scanned PDF: no text to read").

message.description: What to fix, for the user.

v1FoundryFileReadError.description: FoundryFileReadError is why a file can't be read.

v1FoundryFileReadMode.description: FoundryFileReadMode is how deeply a document is read.

v1FoundryFileReadState.description:
FoundryFileReadState is what reading a document has come to.

 - FOUNDRY_FILE_READ_STATE_READY: Ontologies can read it: text, or a file whose read succeeded (a PDF's
text is then on :content).
 - FOUNDRY_FILE_READ_STATE_READING: Being read, or waiting to be (retrying says when after a failure). A
generation started now leaves it out; a load waits for a PDF, and reads
it once its read ends.
 - FOUNDRY_FILE_READ_STATE_FAILED: It can't be read: error says why, and a load records the PDF failed
with the same code. Upload a fixed file.

status.description:
queued, running, succeeded, budget_exhausted, failed or cancelled (a
delete a new load went before, or any job of a deleted ontology).

phase.description: provisioning, ingest, documents or finishing; deleting for a delete.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, written for the customer.

loadId.description: The load it writes or deletes.

v1FoundryGraphJob.description:
FoundryGraphJob is one job on an ontology's database: a load job creates a
load (whose id is its own) from a version's tables, then the documents; an
extract adds documents to a load; a delete removes one.

version.description: The version it writes, as the graph records it: foundry-v<number>.

status.description: writing, ready, partial, failed, deleting or delete_failed.

finishedAt.description: When writing ended; unset while writing.

jobs.description:
Its newest jobs, newest first: at most 20. A current load gains an
extract per upload, so job_count and usd_micros cover all of them.

jobCount.description: How many jobs it has had.

usdMicros.description: What all its jobs spent, in millionths of a US dollar.

ingestViolations.description:
How many violation records its tables left open, as the ingest report
counted them. Unset while writing the tables, and when the report did not
count every chunk (an ingest retried after part of it was written).
Extraction changes the live records, which the graph holds, not this.

origin.description: user, or refresh when a changed table queued it.

enrichment.description: Its People enrichment step; unset when its version enriches no one.

appliedAt.description:
When a refresh last brought its tables up to date in place; unset until
one has.

sources.description:
The snapshot of each table it holds; empty for a load written before
Helix recorded them, or still writing its tables.

v1FoundryLoad.description:
FoundryLoad is one write of an approved version into an ontology's
database. Its id is the id of the load job that creates it, and every node
and edge it writes carries that id as foundry_load, so loads of different
versions sit side by side. Foundry keeps the current load and the newest
others, five in all, and deletes the rest in the background.

status.description:
preparing, queued (waiting for a lookup slot), running, done, partial,
off (the workspace's consent is off: no profiles apply), failed (the
profiles found before apply) or cancelled.

stoppedBy.description:
Why a partial step stopped: cap, provider_credits, provider, time, busy,
stopped (someone stopped the lookups), pro or flag. Unset on any other.

people.description: Everyone of the enriched type the tables hold.

noName.description: Left out with no full name.

noClue.description: Left out with no usable email or LinkedIn URL.

shared.description: Lost a clue another person holds too.

skipped.description: Everyone left out: no_name and no_clue.

carried.description: Reused from an earlier load, at no cost.

toLookUp.description: To be looked up this load.

found.description:
This step's lookups by outcome: found (accepted), held back by the
checks, not found, and unanswered (booked, not resent). A step that
published after its load stopped waiting for it (past its deadline and
the grace) counts what it found then, though the load applied only the
profiles found before; applied and unmatched say what the load applied.

applied.description:
The profiles the load applied that bound their person, and those that
bound no one (the person changed since the lookup); 0 until its tables
are in.

publishedAt.description: When the step published its profiles; unset before.

v1FoundryLoadEnrichment.description:
FoundryLoadEnrichment is a load's People enrichment step: whom it looked up
on context.dev, what it found, and what its profiles bound.

syncId.description:
The sync that wrote the snapshot, and when it finished; both unset for a
load written before Helix recorded them.

v1FoundryLoadSource.description: FoundryLoadSource is the snapshot of one synced table a load holds.

parameterSize.description: Like "4.0B"; empty when the server doesn't say.

unusable.description:
For the owner: why Foundry can't run on it (it calls no tools, its
context window is too small, it runs on ollama.com, it needs a newer
Ollama); empty when it can, or when the server can't say.

v1FoundryOllamaModel.description: FoundryOllamaModel is a model an Ollama server has pulled.

version.description: Its version; empty when it didn't answer.

problem.description:
For the owner: why its models can't be listed, or can't be told apart
(a server too old to say which call tools), and how to fix it; empty
when they can.

v1FoundryOllamaServer.description:
FoundryOllamaServer is what an Ollama server has, as a local install
reads it for Settings › AI models.

projectId.description:
project_id, tenant_id and database_name are empty for a caller who can't
read the project's databases (clusters.read on the project).

lastLoad.description: Its newest load job (kind load); unset before the first.

currentLoad.description:
The load reads go to and uploads are extracted into; unset before a load
finished writing.

activeJob.description:
The job queued or running now, of any kind; unset when none is. The
website polls while it is set.

autoRefresh.description: Whether a changed table reloads the current version by itself.

refreshDueAt.description: When a refresh is owed from; unset when none is.

refreshWaiting.description: Why an owed refresh waits: busy (a job is live); empty otherwise.

v1FoundryOntology.description:
FoundryOntology is a workspace's ontology, bound to one Helix database: a
tenant of one of the workspace's projects. Statuses are the lowercase names
the Foundry contract fixes.

loadId.description: The load it writes or deletes.

phase.description: provisioning, ingest, documents, finishing or deleting.

documents.description:
The uploaded documents its reading version's scope holds: that of the
current load's version, else of the current version; 0 with neither.

version.description: The version it writes, as the graph records it: foundry-v<number>.

status.description: queued, running, succeeded, budget_exhausted, failed or cancelled.

pastDue.description: A paid tier with an unpaid invoice.

currentPeriodEnd.description: End of the paid period; unset on Free.

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: The paid tier ends at current_period_end unless resumed.

code.description: The catalog plan held: free, pro, max or any plan a deployment adds.

v1FoundryPlan.description: FoundryPlan is a workspace's Foundry plan as the billing system reports it now.

null.description: Removes the property; JSON null in the REST API ({"null": null}).

text.description: A string, date (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD) or RFC 3339 datetime.

v1FoundryPropValue.description:
A prop decision's value: null removes the property; any other must be of
the kind the property's type takes, as the engine reads it (no coercion).
integer is an int64, a JSON string in the REST API, so every digit of an
integer past 2^53 is kept.

versionId.description: The load's version, whose definition the agent was given.

threadId.description: The first question of its thread; a new thread's is its own id.

focusJson.description: The entity the user asked about, {"type": ..., "id": ...}; empty for none.

status.description: queued, running, answered, cannot_answer, failed or cancelled.

resultJson.description:
The agent's AskResult as JSON (ask_result.json): set once answered or
cannot_answer, and for a failed question whose agent sent one.

error.description: Why it failed or was retried, for the user.

usdMicros.description: What its attempts spent, in millionths of a US dollar.

lastSeq.description: The seq of its newest event; 0 before any.

attempts.description:
Attempts claimed so far; a queued question with attempts above 0 is
waiting to be retried, and error says why.

reservedMicros.description: What a running question holds back of the month's budget: its cap.

v1FoundryQuestion.description:
FoundryQuestion is one question asked of one load of an ontology. The
foundry-ask-worker answers it with the ontology agent's read-only Ask; its
run streams events (ListFoundryQuestionEvents), then it ends with a result.

monthlyUsdMicros.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

concurrentLimit.description: Per workspace: questions running at once, and asked in an hour.

v1FoundryQuestionBudget.description:
FoundryQuestionBudget is a workspace's questions budget this calendar
month (UTC), apart from its loads', and the caps every question runs
under. A question is refused when what the month spent plus its cap passes
the budget, and waits, queued, while running questions' reservations
leave too little.

eventJson.description:
The agent's event as JSON (ask_event.json): started, tool_call,
tool_result or finished. A retried question's events go on from where
its last attempt's ended, from a new started.

v1FoundryQuestionEvent.description: FoundryQuestionEvent is one event of a question's run, in order from seq 1.

v1FoundryReadKind.description:
FoundryReadKind is how ontologies read a type of document.

 - FOUNDRY_READ_KIND_TEXT: Markdown, MDX and plain text: extracted as text through routes.
 - FOUNDRY_READ_KIND_TABLE: CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL and Parquet: read once, at upload, as a table of
its own, which mappings name by the document's id.
 - FOUNDRY_READ_KIND_PDF: PDF: read once, at upload, to its text (each page's, a form feed
between pages), then extracted as that text through routes. One with no
text layer (a scan), encrypted or damaged can't be read.

notInData.description: Must be true. This explicitly chooses "not in data".

v1FoundryReviewChoice.description: A user choice. Review identity is always derived by the backend.

value.description:
A prop decision's value as stored. A whole number within int64 is an
integer here, even a float property's (3.0 reads back as integer 3).

v1FoundryReviewDecision.description: A durable ontology-wide override; applies from the next load.

everySeconds.description: The automatic sync interval a connector gets unless its owner picks a longer one.

shortestSeconds.description: The shortest interval an owner may pick.

capture.description: Capture methods allowed: full, cursor, events, log.

reconcileEverySeconds.description: How often a table that takes changes is read in full; 0 when every sync is full.

refreshEverySeconds.description: The least time between two refreshes of one ontology.

v1FoundrySyncRules.description: FoundrySyncRules is how often a plan syncs connectors and refreshes graphs.

v1FoundryTier.description:
FoundryTier is a workspace's Helix Foundry plan. Free is the absence of a
paid tier. Max grants everything Pro does.

monthStart.description: The first of the month, 00:00 UTC.

resetsAt.description: The first of the next month, 00:00 UTC, when every cap starts again.

totalUsdMicros.description:
What the month spent: every task's spent once (API_SOURCES is in
LOADS), without questions' reservations.

tasks.description: One entry per task, in FoundryUsageTask's order.

v1FoundryUsage.description:
FoundryUsage is a workspace's AI spend this calendar month (UTC), by task,
with each task's cap: the same sums the caps check. Spend on the
workspace's own model key counts as Helix's does, priced as its AI setting
prices it (nothing for a model on its own hardware): Helix's monthly caps
count it too, as no ledger of own-key spend exists apart from them.

spentUsdMicros.description:
In millionths of a US dollar: what the task's work spent, a running
job's spend so far included.

reservedUsdMicros.description:
What running work holds back of the cap beyond spent: only questions
reserve (a running question's cap). Its cap refuses new work once
spent, reserved and the work's own cap would pass it.

capUsdMicros.description: The month's cap; unset for a task that has none.

v1FoundryUsageTask.description:
FoundryUsageTask is a kind of model work a workspace's month of AI spend
is broken down by (FoundryUsage). Ontology drafts (generations and
revisions) are not among them: they record tokens, not dollars; nor are
generation titles, which record no spend at all.

 - FOUNDRY_USAGE_TASK_LOADS: Loads and extracts of the workspace's ontologies, created this month:
reading documents into their graphs, which is all of a load's model
spend (tables load at no model cost). Capped by foundry.graph.monthly_usd
(config.FoundryGraphConfig.MonthBudget), the budget the graph worker
checks.
 - FOUNDRY_USAGE_TASK_API_SOURCES: What work no person started (refreshes, and extracts no one asked for)
spent extracting the workspace's API sources' pieces this month, its
deleted sources' included. Capped by
foundry.events.max_system_usd_per_workspace_month. Part of LOADS' spend,
so FoundryUsage.total_usd_micros counts it once, there.
 - FOUNDRY_USAGE_TASK_QUESTIONS: Questions charged this month (claimed in it, whenever asked), as the
questions budget counts them (FoundryQuestionBudget). Capped by
foundry.ask.monthly_usd.

mediaType.description: The document's type, as uploaded: what data is.

data.description:
As uploaded, at most foundry.documents.max_bytes (1 MiB); base64 in
JSON.

text.description:
As uploaded, at most the type's cap; bytes that are not UTF-8 read as
U+FFFD. A PDF's is its text as ontologies read it: each page's, with a
form feed (U+000C) between pages, at most 1 MiB.

token.description: Fine-grained (github_pat_…) or classic (ghp_…) personal access token; write-only.

repos.description: owner/name; empty syncs every repository the token reads, up to 100.

reviewDays.description: Reviews are read for pull requests updated in the last this many days, 1 to 365; 0 means 90.

apiKey.description: Granola personal or workspace API key (grn_…); write-only.

transcripts.description:
Also keep each note's transcript as a document, in the connection's
Transcripts set beside its Notes. Off by default.

pendingPieces.description: Pieces in batches no sync has read yet.

v1ListFoundryEventSourceTokensResponse.description: Newest first, revoked ones included, at most 50.

status.description:
The question's status when read: once it is not queued or running and
the events reach last_seq, none follows.

budget.description: The workspace's questions budget this month.

v1OntologyEdit.description: One edit of a version's draft: put an item, or remove one.

v1OntologyFormat.description:
OntologyFormat says what a version's definition holds.

 - ONTOLOGY_FORMAT_FOUNDRY_V1: Entities, relationships, rules and constraints.
 - ONTOLOGY_FORMAT_AGENT_BUNDLE: The ontology agent's draft: format, status, ontology_toml, mappings_toml,
draft, questions, summary and usage.

baseVersionId.description:
The version that was current when it was requested; the draft extends it.
Unset for a revision, whose parent is revision.parent_version_id.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, written for the customer.

resultVersionId.description: The draft it stored, once succeeded. It is not made current.

nextAttemptAt.description: When a queued generation runs next; later than now while a retry waits.

ontologyId.description: The Foundry ontology it drafts a version of.

title.description:
A one-line, plain-text title of the goal, at most 60 characters, for
lists and headings; the goal holds the full text. Empty without a goal and
for generations queued before titles.

documentSetIds.description: The document sets the draft may route to extraction.

revision.description: Set exactly for a revision of a version (ReviseOntologyVersion).

documents.description:
The table files of its document sets it drafts from beside the tables:
each is a table of its own, which mappings name by its document id. A
revision's are its parent's.

sample.description:
The sample it drafts from in place of the AI
(GenerateOntologyRequest.sample); empty for an AI draft.

v1OntologyGeneration.description: OntologyGeneration is one request to draft a version of an ontology.

v1OntologyGenerationDocument.description:
OntologyGenerationDocument is a table file a generation drafts from, and
the set it was in then.

itemId.description: The item, such as rule.overdue or type.Customer; at most 256 bytes.

toml.description: The item's whole TOML snippet. A revision's snippets add up to at most 1 MiB.

v1OntologyPut.description:
Puts an item's TOML snippet in the draft, replacing the item if the draft
has it: an extraction route, a rule, a constraint, or a type's identifiers.

v1OntologyRemove.description: Removes an item from the draft.

dryRun.description: A preview: it stores no version.

resultJson.description:
The engine's result once it ended: status, findings and cards, without
the definition, refusals included. Only GetOntologyGeneration has it.

resultWithheld.description:
True in place of result_json for a caller who can't query the
ontology's database (database.query.read on its project): the result
measures its load, so its cards, counts and findings are withheld.

v1OntologyRevision.description: What a revision generation revises, and what came of it.

definition.description: The definition, in the shape format names; unset in lists.

generationId.description: The generation that wrote it, for generated versions.

isCurrent.description: Whether the ontology points at this version.

ontologyId.description: The Foundry ontology it is a version of.

evidenceWithheld.description:
The definition's draft items were sent without their evidence cards: a
revised version's cards measure the ontology's load, and the caller
can't query its database (database.query.read on its project).

documentSetIds.description:
Its scope: the document sets its loads read. A load's documents are the
uploaded documents of these sets; empty reads none. A generated
version's are the sets its generation picked, a revised one's its
parent's plus the sets its revised routes name; a hand-written
Definition v1 reads none.

v1OntologyVersion.description: OntologyVersion is one immutable ontology of a workspace.

v1OntologyVersionResponse.description: OntologyVersionResponse leaves version unset when the ontology has no current version.

apiKey.description: Personal API key with Query Read and Project Read; write-only.

host.description: HTTPS origin of a self-hosted PostHog; custom region only.

projectId.description: Filled in by a test when the key sees exactly one project.

eventDays.description: Days of events to sync, 1 to 365; 0 means 30.

mode.description: export reads PostHog batch exports from export_bucket; empty reads the query API.

v1ReadFoundryGraphResponse.description:
ReadFoundryGraphResponse is the agent's ReadResult (read_result.json): one
result per read, in order, each its value or its own error.

prefix.description: Folder; empty reads the whole bucket. Ends with "/" once prepared.

region.description: A test fills it in when empty; optional with an endpoint.

tables.description: Tables to sync; empty means every table.

v1S3ConnectorConfig.description: S3ConnectorConfig reads Parquet, JSON, JSON Lines and CSV files from a bucket.

externalId.description: This workspace's; the role's trust policy must require it.

v1S3ConnectorSetup.description: S3ConnectorSetup is what a customer's role must trust.

endpoint.description: HTTPS origin of an S3-compatible store; empty means AWS.

capture.description: How the table is read now: full, cursor, events or log.

v1SyncedTable.description: SyncedTable is one table's newest snapshot.

config.description: The settings as they would be stored, write-only fields empty.
